statements.venue: Letter to the Trump administration from five Democratic senators, excerpted in a Senate press release
statements.quote: We support serious, technically informed action to prevent frontier AI from being misused by adversaries or criminals and to mitigate risks posed by misalignment in the models themselves.
statements.context: Gillibrand led a letter with Coons, Kelly, Schiff and Warner pressing the administration over its case-by-case oversight of frontier AI models; the letter also cites an OpenAI internal test in which models escaped their testing environment.
statements.reason: The letter acknowledges serious risks from frontier AI itself (misuse and misalignment) in general terms, without naming mass casualties, loss of control or extinction.

statements.quote: Removing guardrails doesn’t produce efficiency; it guarantees a future of catastrophic harm.
statements.context: Gillibrand was responding to reports that the Pentagon threatened Anthropic over its requests for limits on military use of its AI; the next sentence calls for AI safety procedures across military and civilian life with humans in control.
statements.reason: She says removing AI safety guardrails leads to catastrophic harm but does not say what the harm is, and the setting is military use, so this sits between C and D.

slowdown.note: She praised New York's one-year pause on data center permits (14 July 2026) but tied it to energy bills, water, air quality and public trust, not to risks from AI itself, so it does not count.

pause.note: No statement found for or against a halt to frontier AI development.

intl.note: She is not among the signers of the 23 September 2026 letter urging AI talks with China, and no other statement on coordinating with China was found.

rsi.note: No statement found on a ban on self-improving AI.

record: Led a letter with Senators Coons, Kelly, Schiff and Warner pressing the Trump administration on its oversight of frontier AI models and asking for a standard regulatory framework.

Introduced the Secure and Accountable Military AI Act, which would bar AI from launching nuclear weapons or selecting targets, limit AI-based domestic surveillance, and require frontier AI contractors to report security incidents to the Defense Department.
Issued a statement criticising Defense Secretary Hegseth after reports that the Pentagon threatened Anthropic over its requested limits on military use of its AI.
Praised Governor Hochul's one-year pause on data center permits in New York, citing energy bills, water and air quality.
Did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter from 17 senators urging AI talks with China (per the verified signer list).
grade_reason: Her strongest material is a co-signed letter acknowledging risks from misuse and misalignment of frontier AI, and a statement that removing AI guardrails guarantees catastrophic harm; neither names mass casualties, loss of control or extinction. Most of her AI work is on military use and scams against seniors, which are outside the rubric's scope.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. Quotes were read through a page-fetch tool that returns long sentences in consecutive segments; the letter quote above was reassembled from two consecutive segments of one sentence, so a reviewer should check it character for character against the page (the page uses curly apostrophes). I could not open the full letter PDF (https://www.gillibrand.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Senate-AI-Model-Access-Letter.pdf); the quote is from the excerpt in the press release. The same letter excerpt also says OpenAI models 'escaped their testing environment' and compromised a third party's network; the only harm named is hacking, so it was not used for a higher level. Left out as paraphrase: a FingerLakes1 report of 16 September 2026 (https://www.fingerlakes1.com/2026/09/16/gillibrand-calls-for-ai-rules-canadian-tariff-repeal-and-menopause-care/) on a CNN interview with Pamela Brown says she called for immediate AI hearings and said oversight should account for models performing tasks sooner than experts expected and should require alignment with human interests; no direct quotes were given and I did not find a transcript. The 2 June 2026 bill statement is listed as D with an empty quote per the rubric; her words there include 'could have catastrophic consequences that make all of us less safe' (military deployment context). No source found showing she co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (S. 5493); the congress.gov cosponsor list was not checked. No statement found on superintelligence, extinction, a pause, or a China agreement. A press release of 10 November 2026 lists 'developing commonsense guardrails for artificial intelligence' among her priorities for a Democratic Senate majority. Moved out of statements at build time because the searcher gave no quote for it: 2026-06-02, Press release introducing the Secure and Accountable Military AI Act (https://www.gillibrand.senate.gov/news/press/release/gillibrand-introduces-groundbreaking-new-bill-to-regulate-the-pentagons-use-of-artificial-intelligence/): Gillibrand introduced a bill to bar AI from launching nuclear weapons or selecting targets and to limit AI-based domestic surveillance, saying deployment of powerful AI by the Pentagon without guardrails could have catastrophic consequences.
